Your data

Tesserae privacy policy

Last updated: 15 November 2026

Tesserae is an Android app for keeping your household’s loyalty and membership cards on your phone. It is made by Miltiadis Sitaridis. This policy explains what data the app handles and why. Miltiadis Sitaridis is responsible for that data (the “controller” under the EU General Data Protection Regulation, GDPR) and can be reached at tesserae.support@gmail.com.

Without an account

Tesserae works fully without an account. Your cards, their photos, how often you use them and your settings stay on your phone and are never sent anywhere, except to your own Garmin watch if you choose to (below).

With a Google account

You can sign in with Google to sync your cards between your phones and to share cards with your household in a Shared Space. When you sign in, Tesserae’s server stores:

  • your first name and Google account ID, which Google provides when you sign in, to identify your account (the server keeps only your first name, not your full name). Google also gives the app your email address so Settings can show which account you signed in with, but the server does not keep it;
  • the cards you keep in your account and in Shared Spaces: name, nickname, card number, barcode format, country, store and notes;
  • the card photos you add, at most 20 per account: a photo of the card that is shown as the card’s tile;
  • which Shared Spaces you belong to, and your role in them;
  • which of your cards you pinned, so your pins come back on a new or reinstalled phone. Only you see them, never the other members of a Shared Space.

These are used only to sync your cards and to show your first name to the other members of a Shared Space you join. They are never sold, never used for advertising and never shared with anyone else, apart from the services that run Tesserae for us (below). The members of a Shared Space see that Space’s cards and the first names of its members.

How often you use each card and your settings always stay on your phone, even when you are signed in.

Please don’t put sensitive information, such as health details, in a card’s notes or photo: they sync to your phones and to the other members of a Shared Space.

Garmin watch

If you use the Tesserae watch app, Send to watch in Settings sends your pinned cards to your Garmin watch: for each card its name, card number and barcode format, at most 50 cards. They go from your phone to your watch over Bluetooth, through the Garmin Connect app on your phone, and are stored on the watch so you can show them at the till. Nothing is sent unless you tap Send to watch, and it needs no account. Tesserae sends nothing to Garmin’s servers, and the watch app sends nothing back. Sending again replaces the cards on the watch; removing the watch app from the watch removes them. The Garmin Connect app itself is Garmin’s, under Garmin’s own privacy policy.

Household unlock purchase

Creating a Shared Space needs the one-time Household unlock, bought in the app through Google Play. Google Play handles the payment under its own terms and privacy policy: we never see your card or bank details, your address or your Google Play account.

When you buy, the app tells Google Play a code made from your Tesserae account (a one-way hash of the account ID, which Google can’t turn back into the ID), so the purchase belongs to your Tesserae account. Tesserae’s server then asks Google Play whether the purchase is paid and stores on your account that you have the unlock, when you got it, and Google Play’s order number. The order number is used only to tell when a purchase was refunded, so the unlock can end. Members of your Shared Space never see whether or what you paid.

Google Play also sends us monthly sales reports with each order’s number, product, price and date, and the buyer’s country (for some countries also region and postal code), but no name or contact details. We keep them as long as tax law requires (7 years in the Netherlands).

Why we may use this data

Tesserae keeps this data to give you the service you sign up for: syncing and sharing your cards, and the Household unlock you bought (GDPR article 6(1)(b), performance of a contract). Sales reports are kept because tax law requires it (article 6(1)(c), legal obligation). Nothing is used for any other purpose.

Where the data is kept

The server runs on Microsoft Azure in the West Europe region (the Netherlands). Data is encrypted in transit (HTTPS) and at rest. The services that help run Tesserae are:

  • Microsoft Azure hosts the server and its database, under Microsoft’s data protection terms;
  • Google handles sign-in, and Google Play distributes the app and handles payments for the Household unlock, each under Google’s own privacy policy;
  • Garmin’s Garmin Connect app carries the cards you send to your own watch, if you use one (above);
  • GitHub hosts this website, which keeps the usual web server logs.

The data is stored in the EU. Microsoft and Google are certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework for any access from outside the EU.

What Tesserae does not collect

  • No ads, analytics or crash-reporting services.
  • No location.
  • Camera and photos: the camera scans a card’s barcode, and those images are processed on the phone and never stored or sent. A card photo you take or choose yourself is cropped and saved again on the phone, which removes its location and camera details, before it is stored. It is sent to the server only while you are signed in.
  • Diagnostic log: kept on your phone. It leaves the phone only if you share it yourself, and it never contains card numbers.

Keeping and deleting your data

Your data is kept while you use your account. When you delete a card, the server keeps only a marker that tells your other phones and your Shared Space to remove it too: the card’s name, number, notes and other details are erased at once, and its photo is deleted. The marker itself is deleted 30 days later. The same goes for a deleted Shared Space and for leaving one: the record that you were a member is deleted 30 days after you left.

A card photo is deleted from the server when you remove or replace it. If that ever doesn’t reach the server, a photo that no card uses is deleted after 7 days anyway. An invite code is deleted 7 days after it was made or used.

If you don’t sign in to Tesserae for 2 years (an app in use renews its sign-in about once a month), your account and its data are deleted from the server, as if you had deleted it yourself. We can’t warn you first, since we don’t keep your email address. An account stays as long as someone still uses a Shared Space it owns, so your household doesn’t lose its cards. An account with the Household unlock, bought or kept free from before it, is deleted this way only after 5 years without a sign-in, so you don’t lose what you paid for if you come back later. Delete it yourself whenever you like.

Deleting your account also deletes the record of your Household unlock; the unlock ends with it.

You can sign out at any time and choose to keep your cards on the phone or remove them. To delete your account and the data on the server, use Settings → Delete account in the app, or see Delete your account.

The database makes automatic backups, each kept for about 8 hours, so deleted data is gone from them within about 8 hours too.

Android may also back up the app’s cards and card photos to your Google account, as it does for most apps, so a new phone gets them back. This backup is Google’s, encrypted with your phone’s screen lock, and you can turn it off in Android’s settings.

Your rights

You can ask for a copy of your data, have it corrected or deleted, ask us to limit or stop using it, and receive it in a format you can take elsewhere. Most of this you can do in the app itself: edit or delete cards, Export cards in Settings for a copy of your cards, sign out, or delete your account. For anything else, such as a copy of everything the server holds about you, email tesserae.support@gmail.com with your account id (Settings → Account → Copy account id); you get an answer within one month.

If you think your data is mishandled, you can complain to the Dutch data protection authority, the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens, or to the authority of the EU country where you live.

Children

Tesserae is meant for people aged 16 and over.

Changes

If this policy changes, the new version is published on this page with a new date.

Contact

Questions about privacy: tesserae.support@gmail.com
